## Findings
- claim-1: Conditional on the accepted integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation, for \(c=r-j=1\), \(p=q-i\ge2\), and \(\min(i,j)=2\), with \(d=ij\), \[ Q_d\oplus Q_{d+1}\oplus Q_{d+2} \cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2, \] where \[ x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}. \] Moreover \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\) and \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\), for \[ y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},\qquad y_2=s_{(i^j,2)}. \]
- claim-2: The requested opposite-boundary truncated certificate is established: retaining \(x_2\), the complementary minor on columns \((u,z,y_2)\) has determinant \(1\), where \[ u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})},\qquad z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)}. \]
## Strategy
Assume the accepted integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation. Put \(d=ij\). For \(c=1,\ p\ge2\), the degree-\(d+2\) columns are
\[
(u,x_2,z,y_2),
\]
since \(w\) is outside the box. The complete Pieri rows are
\[
u+z+y_2,\qquad u+x_2+z,\qquad z+y_2.
\]
Retaining \(x_2\), the complementary minor on \((u,z,y_2)\) is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1&1\\
1&1&0\\
0&1&1
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det=1.
\]
Thus the row lattice is unimodularly complementary to \(x_2\). Together with \(x_1+y_1=0\) in degree \(d+1\), this gives
\[
Q_d\oplus Q_{d+1}\oplus Q_{d+2}
\cong
\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2,
\]
with \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\) and \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\).

The requested opposite-boundary truncated certificate is established.

## Gaps
This is conditional on the accepted integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation and proves nothing in degrees \(>d+2\). It does not establish the all-degree quotient, generation, or minimality.

## Next
Any all-degree elimination or graded-kernel argument must be treated separately.
